opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers in the humanities or social sciences based at a UK university or recognised research organisation; UK or EEA citizens (or any nationality with a UK doctorate) who have completed their viva between 1 Apr 2024 and 1 Apr 2027; must be at early‑career/post‑doctoral stage and not hold a permanent academic post.
opportunities.summary: Three‑year fellowships to support early‑career researchers to undertake independent, publishable research in the humanities or social sciences.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK‑based researchers with a long‑term appointment at a UK higher‑education institution or independent research organisation; must be conducting original research in the humanities or social sciences; early‑career, mid‑career and senior researchers eligible; co‑applicants may be UK or overseas.
opportunities.summary: Funding of up to £10,000 for 6‑12 months to develop quantitative, data‑science, digital‑humanities, language or other methodological skills and to disseminate them.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK‑based early‑career or mid‑career researchers in the humanities or social sciences; no specific disciplinary restriction; must be able to work in Berlin at DGAP.
opportunities.summary: One‑year fellowships (up to £150,000) to develop skills, networks and policy‑relevant research in security, defence, Indo‑European relations, technology/AI, or strategy‑making.

opportunities.title: APEX Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a permanent or fixed‑term UK university or not‑for‑profit research organisation position; must be able to lead interdisciplinary collaboration across at least two Academy remits (Humanities/Social Sciences, Engineering, Natural Sciences).
opportunities.summary: Seed funding (up to £200,000) for up to 24‑month interdisciplinary projects that bring together the British Academy, Royal Society and Royal Academy of Engineering.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any UK‑based researcher (early‑career to senior) in the humanities or social sciences; must partner with a GLAM or performing‑arts organisation; cannot have previously received this award.
opportunities.summary: Public‑engagement projects (up to £8,000) to develop innovative ways of sharing humanities/social‑science research with audiences in partnership with museums, galleries, archives or performing‑arts venues.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK‑based principal investigators in the humanities or social sciences with a permanent role; must collaborate with overseas co‑applicants; interdisciplinary across SHAPE or STEM disciplines.
opportunities.summary: Projects (up to £300,000) to investigate mobilities (people, materials, ideas) through genuinely interdisciplinary international collaborations.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs Funding
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Current British Academy award‑holders or applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award within the next six months; must meet eligibility for the target scheme.
opportunities.summary: Small grants to cover equipment, caring costs, accessibility support or assistance needed to prepare or carry out a British Academy award application or award.

opportunities.title: Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 (Alexander von Humboldt Foundation)

amount.raw: seed funding provided to participants (covers travel, accommodation, visa costs)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early‑career researchers in the humanities or social sciences affiliated with UK or German research institutions.
opportunities.summary: Funding for up to ~15 UK and 15 German early‑career researchers to attend a three‑day interdisciplinary symposium on ‘Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future’, with seed funding for collaborative follow‑up projects.
